presentation.label: No stray locks after removing one
presentation.summary: Removing a parameter or scene lock with a knob press no longer writes a new lock when the knob slips a detent.
presentation.overview: On the MKII, pressing a DATA ENTRY knob while holding a trig (or SCENE A/B) removes that lock when you let go. A finger that nudges the knob while pressed turns the removal into a coarse x7 jump, and one that nudges it on release writes a new lock. Butter Fingers ignores the first slipped detent while the knob is pressed and every detent for 150 ms after its release, only while a lock is being edited. Deliberate coarse edits still work, one detent later.
highlights: Only while a TRIG key or SCENE A/B is held, and only for the pressed knob: everything else behaves as stock.
The release window is 150 ms; a deliberate turn right after it is not delayed.
Press + turn still makes stock's coarse x7 edit, starting from the second detent.
No setting, no stock code patched, nothing stored in the project.
usage: Hold a TRIG key with a parameter lock and press the DATA ENTRY knob of the locked parameter; let go. The lock is removed, as in stock.
Let go of the knob carelessly, nudging it a detent as you lift your finger: with Butter Fingers the lock stays removed instead of a new lock being written.
For a deliberate coarse edit, keep the knob pressed and turn it: the first detent is ignored, from the second on it moves in stock's coarse steps (x7).
Scene locks work the same way: hold SCENE A or B and press the knob to remove that scene's lock.

access.location: Every page with DATA ENTRY knobs, while a TRIG key or SCENE A/B is held
steps: Hold a TRIG key with a parameter lock and press the DATA ENTRY knob of the locked parameter; let go. The lock is removed, as in stock.
Let go of the knob carelessly, nudging it a detent as you lift your finger: with Butter Fingers the lock stays removed instead of a new lock being written.
For a deliberate coarse edit, keep the knob pressed and turn it: the first detent is ignored, from the second on it moves in stock's coarse steps (x7).
Scene locks work the same way: hold SCENE A or B and press the knob to remove that scene's lock.

limitations: OS 1.40C, MKII (the MKI has no knob presses). Reported on one MKII only.
Changes a stock gesture while a lock is edited: the first detent of press + turn and every detent for 150 ms after the knob's release are ignored. Remove the module to restore stock behaviour.
A detent turned just before the press registers reaches the firmware; the press then removes the lock it wrote.
LEVEL and press + turn outside lock editing are untouched.

storage.label: Runtime package
storage.display: 544 B code and data + 44 B state
storage.conditions: sdk/runtime/loader/build.py --octabam, one ColdFire unit, three runtime hooks, 4 relocations, no stock-code sites, no DSP code.

processing.label: ColdFire, per key, knob turn and UI tick
processing.conditions: A few compares and bit operations per key or turn, one increment per UI tick (60 a second). Nothing per sample or frame.

impact.conditions: UI task: key and encoder events and the 60 Hz tick.

cpu.rationale: Tens of ColdFire instructions per panel event and a counter per UI tick; no audio-path work.

memory.rationale: A 544-byte unit and 44 bytes of state.

tests.summary: Host gate (verify.py, 20 checks) and an ot_emu lock-removal comparison against stock on the beta base cd39c494 over emulated USB; reported working on one MKII over USB. No owner-verified hardware qualification yet.
